xwhatsapp-strokecopylinkgoogleAdd Al Jazeera on GoogleinfoBrazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro disembarks from a plane after arriving at Opa-Locka executive airport near Miami, Florida, the United States, October 28, 2026 [Eva Marie Uzcategui/Reuters]By APPublished On 28 Oct 202628 Oct 2026Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro has issued a statement hours after arriving in Miami, in the United States, with his family, days after losing a presidential election to incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, and claimed he was “the true elected president of Brazil”.

The far-right politician thanked US President Donald Trump. Bolsonaro said the allegations of embezzlement and money laundering against him were “a politically motivated witch-hunt, intended to hold me hostage”. He also claimed without evidence that the election results were fraudulent.

“Faced with the politicization of the justice system in Brazil, I brought my family to the US. I did not flee Brazil; I left for Brazil’s sake. I left a state of exception so that I could be the leader my people deserve,” he said.

Bolsonaro asked the international community “not to normalize what is happening in Brazil” and said he would lead the country’s opposition from the US.

Dressed casually in a dark polo shirt and flanked by his wife and two daughters, Bolsonaro stepped out of the plane shortly after it landed at about 9:30am local time (13:30 GMT). Florida, where Miami is located, is home to the largest population of Brazilians in the United States.

Al Jazeera’s John Holman, reporting from outside Opa-Locka executive airport, where the family landed on Wednesday morning, said the group was “whisked away in an SUV” from the airport soon after arriving.

Brazil‘s Supreme Court had ordered Bolsonaro to surrender his regular and diplomatic passports shortly after the election, in an attempt to make sure the right-wing senator did not flee the country before he could be investigated for embezzlement and money laundering.

As a senator, Bolsonaro had immunity from potential criminal prosecution, but he would lose that protection in January, since he gave up his seat to run for president.

Holman said the Bolsonaro family’s flight from Brazil was a dramatic escape, starting with crossing into neighbouring Argentina “on a rope bridge, on foot”.

Argentine immigration authorities said the senator and his family entered the country late on Tuesday night, and less than an hour later boarded a private plane operated by Baires Fly destined for Guayaquil, Ecuador.

That plane arrived in Ecuador, and later took off for Miami, Florida, with Bolsonaro and his family on board.

Both Ecuador and Argentina are run by right-wing leaders who are close allies of US President Donald Trump, said Holman. The countries provided “stepping stones among allies”, and the US Department of State issued visas for the family.

Brazil and the US do have an extradition treaty, but Holman said it is expected Bolsonaro will be protected by Trump, who said yesterday the Bolsonaro family were “fine people”.

“The signs are, with the State Department issuing him a visa, with the comments coming from President Trump, that they’re not gonna be in any hurry to hand him back to Brazil,” Holman said.

Flavio’s father, Brazil’s former President Jair Bolsonaro, undertook a very similar journey to Florida after he lost his bid for re-election in 2022. While he was in the US, the elder Bolsonaro’s supporters attempted to orchestrate a coup. He later returned to Brazil and is currently under house arrest there.
